name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: I’ll pull Eitan’s latest design picks from the shared drive (folder: `/design-references/eitan-picks/2024-q2/`), then extract the top 10 most-tweeted/liked visuals into a single PDF (`eitan-picks-top10-2024q2.pdf`) for quick taste-learning. After that, I’ll run a 5-minute visual audit on Mine AI’s current homepage (`/mine-ai-web/src/index.html`) to flag gaps against Eitan’s style cues.

name: Squint
text: Squint: Hold on—Easel’s plan assumes *tweet/like counts* correlate with *design quality* or *Mine AI’s needs*, but engagement ≠ efficacy. Where’s the evidence that Eitan’s most viral picks align with our product’s constraints (e.g., loading speed, accessibility)? Also, a 5-minute audit on a *static* PDF won’t catch UX flaws in a live site—demand a real performance test or user-flow review.

name: Easel
text:
Easel: I’ll pivot to a *design-quality-first* approach—pulling Eitan’s picks from `/design-references/eitan-picks/2024-q2/` and filtering for *visual principles* (contrast, hierarchy, motion efficiency) via a 20-minute heuristic audit (tools: Figma’s Contrast Checker, Lighthouse for performance). I’ll compile the top 10 *high-quality* picks into `eitan-picks-quality-2024q2.pdf` with annotated notes, then run a 10-minute audit on Mine AI’s `/src/components/hero-banner.tsx` for real-world constraints. Artifact: annotated PDF + audit report.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-6618, worker-9022 — done, dissolved]

name: Squint
text: Squint: Easel’s pivot to *visual principles* still skips the core risk—heuristic audits (even 20-minute ones) can’t substitute for *user-task alignment*. Where’s the evidence that contrast/hierarchy/motion efficiency in Eitan’s picks actually improve *Mine AI’s* conversion or retention metrics? And Lighthouse’s performance scores are a blunt instrument—have we validated that "efficient motion" (e.g., micro-interactions) doesn’t harm accessibility for low-vision users? Show me the data tying these heuristics to *our* product’s goals, or this is just aesthetic guesswork.
